title: The Person Who Wrote Chopsticks Was a 16-Year-Old Girl
hook: In 1877, 16-year-old Euphemia Allan of Britain published this tune under a man's name

open.title: The sheet music for this famous tune credits a composer who never existed
open.line: You can play it without knowing how to play piano. But the composer printed on the score was nobody real. Who really wrote it?

summary: Chopsticks was published in 1877 by 16-year-old Euphemia Allan under a pen name. Its original title was The Celebrated Chop Waltz, and it is the only piece she ever had published.

text: Even people who can't play piano can play a tune with just two fingers.
It's the one known as Chopsticks.
The composer's name printed on the 1877 score was Arthur de Lulli.

panels.text: Must be some famous composer from abroad.

text: In fact, it was a fake name used by Euphemia Allan, a 16-year-old girl from Britain.

panels.mean: The chop in the original title, Chop Waltz. It means to strike downward.

text: The score told players to turn both hands on their sides, little fingers down, and play.
That hand motion, chopping down on the keys, became the name of the piece.

panels.text: So it's not about chopsticks, it's a tune you chop out with the side of your hand.

text: It's the only piece she ever had published.
The publisher who put out the score was her brother.
